author: Zeno Ren

first_attempt.cause_detail: Role lb-release-controller-target granted get on secrets with resourceNames limited to claude-lb-copilot-auth. The pod template gained a second secret reference (claude-lb-credential-key) during pre-release preparation, so preflight's _verify_references could not read it.

remediation.change: added claude-lb-credential-key to the existing secrets rule resourceNames
remediation.method: kubectl apply of the object rebuilt from its own last-applied-configuration, so the apply-managed state stays consistent
remediation.reads_digest_only: _verify_references compares digest({data,binaryData,type,immutable}) against the plan snapshot; no secret value is persisted

probe_model_choice: databricks-claude-opus-5 rather than opus-5-5, which is intermittently capacity-limited upstream and caused the 2026-10-10 rollback when used as a mandatory gate

configmap_change.reason: the previously running image c318724 does not parse `enabled`, so applying before the release would have made the four accounts live wildcards in any window where the old pod restarted
configmap_change.validated_before_apply: merged YAML parsed and compared field by field; existing endpoints byte-identical, other config sections identical, no token material added
configmap_change.takes_effect: next rolling restart; the running pod still holds 1 Copilot endpoint because config is read at startup only

build.dependency_verification: each wheel's local sha256 compared against the value published by the PyPI JSON API, because the wheelhouse is populated through a corporate proxy index rather than the PyPI file CDN

no_migration_required: copilot_account_policy had never existed in production (key_policy.py is absent from c318724), so widening its enabled column to NULL-able is a first creation rather than a migration
outstanding: The four Copilot accounts appear in the Dashboard only after the next rolling restart; they are inert and nothing depends on them.
Enabling each one requires discover -> select models -> enable, then one further restart before it serves traffic.
Azure Foundry credentials still return 401 on every path and have served zero requests. The v1 GA switch in PR #33 does not address that; the credentials themselves need replacing.
Per-key model->provider preference, per-key Copilot account selection, and freezing the routing decision per request are not implemented.
